Commentary.Commentary: Pakistan, Sarfraz Ahmed particularly, would be disappointed with their efforts with the ball and more with how they did in the field. Some sloppy work gave runs away and there were a couple of dropped chances as well. The bowlers couldn't stamp their authority on what has been a dwindling Zimbabwe batting line-up. The performance wasn't bad as such, but given their quality, they'd feel that for sure. Now, the target in front of them won't be an easy one to chase for sure. The second half should be an interesting one. Don't go anywhere, it'll begin shortly...

The hosts have a fighting total on the board courtesy a Solomon Mire masterclass. Zimbabwe, being put into bat, started off well as Zhuwao and Mire gave them a solid start. The former departed, but the latter held one end and kept the runs coming. Stitched good stands, first with his skipper Hamilton, and then went on to add 64 with Musakanda, who himself played a useful cameo. Zimbabwe crossed the 160-mark, but Mire fell 6 short of what would have been a well-deserved ton.
Length ball moving away from around off, Chigumbura punches it through the covers and takes a single. ZIMBABWE FINISH ON 162/4!
Malcolm Waller to bat next.

OUT! Musakanda holes out! Full on the stumps, he clears his front leg trying to clear long on. Doesn't exactly get underneath it, so hits it straight down the throat of the experienced veteran Shoaib Malik. He takes it safely in his hands and dismisses Tarisai. A good cameo from him ends.
Not the shot you want to be playing at this stage, Tarisai. Dot balls are crucial now. Amir spears it fuller outside off, Musakanda looks to bring out the reverse sweep but misses.
Outside off, played well through backward point. Two good runs taken.

FOUR! Streaky runs but they're all the same for the home side. Shortish ball around off, Musakanda swings across the line and gets a thick edge over third man. Clears the man well inside the rope and goes across the fence on a few bounces.
Full ball attacking the stumps, flicked through the mid-wicket region for an easy single.
Mohammad Amir called back into the attack.
Drilled down the ground to long off for one run. A successful over from Talat comes to an end.
Wide! Banged in short but it's too short from Talat, Chigumbura looks to ramp it across the third man fence but misses. Wide called.
On the shorter side of the length, outside off, Chigumbura smacks it through the gap in the covers and gets a brace for doing so.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman down to long off. Single taken.
Wide! Down the leg side, wide signalled by the umpire.
Back of a length close to off, Musakanda lofts it over extra cover and takes two.
Elton Chigumbura walks into the middle next.

OUT! Gone this time. Shadab manages to hold on. That dropped chance hasn't cost Pakistan much. Mire misses out on a ton, but he did what he had to. Departs having scored Zimbabwe's highest individual score in this format. Short ball banged in, Mire pulls this over mid-wicket. Not enough power on it and it's taken well by the leggie coming in from the deep. Mire is gone on 94.

The move almost paid off! Oh dear. Talat bowls a full toss on the stumps, Mire swings and gets a big, big top edge. It goes high in the air towards square, where Asif Ali comes running in from the deep. Settles under it, but fluffs it horribly. Two runs taken. Sarfraz is not a happy man clearly.
Hussain Talat into the bowling attack. Strange or bold move? Remains to be seen.
Lofted over wide mid on, towards the man in the deep on a bounce. Single taken.

This is good running. Mire drills it to long on and sets off for the first run hard. A bit dangerous but he calls for the second and gets to the other end. His partner responded well too. Nicely done.
Fires a yorker outside off, Mire tries to bludgeon it down the ground but fails to make connection.
Shortens his length a bit now, it's swung across the line in front of square leg for a run.

FOUR! Consecutive boundaries for Musakanda. This is superb batting. Full again, fraction straighter in line, Musakanda clears his front leg and once again, staying steady, he whacks it straight back down the ground to find the fence.

FOUR! Hasan Ali welcomed with a boundary yet again. Extremely full, on off, Musakanda stays leg side, keeps his head straight and smacks it through the left of wide mid off for a boundary. Better from him.
Hasan Ali will roll his arm over again.
Tarisai drives this fuller length ball through to long on and retains strike. The 50-run stand is up with this. Handy partnership for Zimbabwe.
Fullish in length and outside the line of off stump, a swipe from the batsman which misses.

Not sure if this is needed from Mire. He can hit 'em well enough in front of the stumps. He moves across his sticks to play the scoop shot, ends up getting it off the edge onto his body. Single taken as the ball falls on the off side.

Big swing and a miss! Fuller and swinging back in, Mire stays firm and swings wildly in an attempt to clear the leg side boundary. Makes no connection though as it goes past the inner edge and the leg pole.
Another length delivery from the bowler, this time Mire stays inside the crease and blocks it out.
On a length on middle and off, shaping back in, it's tucked through backward square leg. Big gap out there, so the batsmen are comfortably able to take two.
Faheem Ashraf is brought back into the attack.
Stump-to-stump line from Amir this time. Much better from him as he keeps it full. Mire drives it to mid off and can only manage a single. 10 off the over. Good one for the hosts.
For a second time in this innings, a different ball has been called for. Both times when Solomon Mire has knocked it out of the park.

SIX! That's outta here! Right out of the screws from Solomon Mire. Whoa! Massive, massive blow. Another slower one from Amir but he's bowled it short. Cannot do that against Mire as he's so strong with those. He stands tall and powers it onto the roof and out of the stadium over square leg. Monstrous hit.
Amir takes the pace off this one and it kind of foxes Musakanda. He swings his bat too early and the ball flies off the edge down to third man on a couple of bounces. One run taken.
Outside off, slanting away, Musakanda plays and misses.

Almost a yorker from Amir. Just outside off. Mire digs it out powerfully back down the track, but much to his dismay, it hits the stumps at the other end. A single is taken eventually as the ball ricochets towards long off, but it could have been a boundary instead. Unlucky.
Closes the face of the bat and works it through mid-wicket for one run.
Mohammad Amir is back.
Flighted delivery on leg stump, Solomon is down to play the reverse sweep, and misses as it goes off his pads on the leg side.
Follows him as he tries to make room, Mire still manages to force it through the covers with his power. Two taken as the man in the deep mops it up.
Darted full and flat on middle and leg, dug out by bringing his bat down in time.
Drifting in, keeps coming in with the angle, Mire hangs his bat out in defense thinking it will turn, but it goes past his inside edge, past the leg stump into the keeper's gloves.

SIX! No stopping him today, is there? He's hitting the ball with so much ease. Teeing off now. Full, loopy and right in the slot, Solomon Mire plants his front foot forward and smokes it deep into the long on stands for half a dozen.
Plays this with the spin and runs it down to third man for one. Brings Mire back on strike.
Mohammad Nawaz returns to the attack.
That's in the air but lands safe. Length ball kicking off the surface, Mire lofts it off the outer half, with not much control, over point. Clears the infield and picks up two runs for it.
Bumper this time, another occasion on which Hasan Ali hits the deck hard. Mire ducks and evades.
Short of a good length, Hasan hits the deck hard, Musakanda punches it firmly down the ground, towards long on for a run.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Just behind a length, on the stumps, heaved away through mid-wicket. There are two men out in the deep, so the batsmen only take two.
Fullish in length and quite close to off, Musakanda leans forward and across before pushing it through to long on for a run.
Hasan Ali back on.
Pushed away nicely past the bowler, through mid off for a single.

Length delivery around off, skids off the deck a bit too and angles in as Mire looks to put bat on ball. Gets an inside edge onto his pads and then the ball rolls away behind on  the off side. Single taken.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Forces this back of a length delivery through the vacant spaces in the cover region and comes back for the second.
FOUR! Back of a length delivery in line of the stumps, Musakanda swivels to get inside the line and then pulls it with aplomb across the mid-wicket fence.

Safe! Comfortably too. Mire taps this towards point and calls for the run. The fielder quickly gets to the ball and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end, as Solomon drags his bat in. It's taken upstairs and replays show that he's in with no problem.
Direct hit! Mire the man in the limelight. Let's see now...
Faheem Ashraf to have a go with the ball again.
The batsman plays the pull shot. They pick up a single.

FOUR! Where does he manage to generate such power from? Superb. Short and outside off, Solomon Mire wastes no time in going back and muscles this through the cover area, beating the two men out in the deep.
FOUR! Stupendous hit! Short from the leggie, Mire instantly rocks back and pulls it with a lot of might through the mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Well outside off, left alone by Mire.
Leans ahead and knocks it through mid on for one. Musakanda is off the mark.
Tarisai Musakanda is the new man in.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Shadab gets rid of the Zimbabwean skipper. Masakadza had no clue about that. The googly from Shadab, Hamilton comes forward to play at it and doesn't read it at all. Right through the gap between bat and pad and the leg stump has been disturbed. Pakistan pick up their second wicket.

Shout for a leg before, but that's never going to be given. Quicker through the air from Nawaz, but it's shorter in length, catches Mire too high on the thigh pad so the umpire never shows interest in the appeal.
Stays back and keeps it out with a straight blade.
Drifting in on leg, it goes off Mire's pads as he attempts to work it on the leg side.
FOUR! Shot. He's cutting loose properly now. Short and wide outside off, Mire looking at the width immediately cuts this hard. Cracks it through point and finds the fence with ease.

SIX! And that's fifty for Solomon Mire! His first in this format. Superb way to bring it up. This is a bit slower through the air, on middle and leg with a lot of flight. Mire throws his front leg out of the way and smokes it high and handsome over long on for a biggie.
Short and fast outside off, played back to the bowler from within the crease.
Floated on the stumps, lofted towards long off for one. 72/1 at the halfway mark!
SIX! Banged short in line of the stumps, Mire camps back and pulls it way over deep mid-wicket for half a dozen.
WIDE! Tossed up well outside off, Mire lets it be.
Flatter outside off, Mire looks to cut but misses.

HE IS SAFE! Hamilton Masakadza. Mire flicks this through square leg and wants two immediately. The fielder in the deep gets to the ball quickly and fires a throw to the bowler. Shadab collects the ball and disturbs the stumps, even as Masakadza stretches to make it in. The appeal is taken upstairs. Replays find that he has managed to drag his bat in.
A run out appeal against Hamilton Masakadza is referred upstairs. Looks close, but think he might be safe.
A change of balls. Solomon Mire hit that so big that the ball was lost. The umpire had to call for a new one.
SIX! Beautifully struck! Tossed up ball in line of the stumps, Mire clears his front leg and smites it high over long on.
Flighted outside off, driven nicely through covers for one.
Shadab Khan has a change of ends.
Guides this down to short third man with the spin. Straight to the fielder so it's a dot ball.
Tossed up from Nawaz, blocked off the front foot by the batsman.

FOUR! That went to the fence in a flash! Superb stuff from Solomon Mire. Looped up, on the stumps, right in the slot and Mire needs no second invitation to put this away. Clears his front leg and hammers it straight back past the diving bowler for a boundary.
On the shorter side once more, Masakadza turns it in front of square on the leg side and crosses over.
Goes back to this short one, deep in the crease and then offers a solid punch to long on for a single.
Short and flat around off, punched off the back foot towards covers.
Mohammad Nawaz comes on to roll his arm over.
Outside off on a length, Masakadza looks to guide it towards third man but gets beaten.
On a length around off, Masakadza defends it from the crease.
Zimbabwe captain Hamilton Masakadza walks in at the fall of the first wicket.

OUT! Castled! Faheem Ashraf provides his skipper the much-needed breakthrough. He lands it full around leg, Zhuwao backs away to hit it through the on side. Misses the ball completely, only to find his leg stump uprooted. An impatient knock from the southpaw comes to an end. This was an innings full of many attempted strokes yet very little to show in the end. The opening stand for Zimbabwe ends one short of a half ton.
Short ball around leg, Cephas looks to pull. Misses and the ball raps him on the unmentionable area. He crouches low in pain, but looks good to carry on.
This ball is punched off the back foot through covers for one.
On a length around leg, Zhuwao backs away and pushes it towards covers for one.
This ball is punched off the back foot towards covers. An excellent beginning from Shadab.
Finally a run! Flatter on the pads, worked away through square leg for one.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball but fails. This has now happened four times in a row.
Another wrong 'un floated outside off, Zhuwao looks to push it down the ground but misses.
Googly outside off, Cephas looks to smash it but misses.
Khan tosses it up outside off, Zhuwao attempts the sweep but misses.
Shadab Khan to roll his arm over now.
SIX! Banged! Short in length around off, Mire swivels and pulls it. Makes a wonderful contact and the ball sails well over the deep backward square leg fence.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads. One run added to the total.

This one is pulled to the on side in front of square. The fielder from mid-wicket, Sohail, gets there and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. The single is completed with ease. Rameez Raja on air states that the Pakistan fielders are standing at the edge of the circle. My colleague pings me that the Aussies were constantly charging in, thereby reducing the opportunities to run singles. Thus, the Asian team seems to be a bit defensive so far.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
On a length outside off, Mire looks to pull it across the line but misses.
On a length around off, pulled away on the bounce to mid-wicket.
Faheem Ashraf is introduced into the attack.
Full and outside off, Zhuwao misses yet again after having a slash.
This one is flicked away through square leg for one.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.

Misfield from Shadab at backward point! Mire pushes it there from the crease, but the fielder lets it through. Asif Ali gets to his right from third man, but doesn't pick the ball up on a go. Thus, another couple is possible, not pleasing the Pakistan captain.
This one is pulled away through backward square leg for a brace.

FOUR! Smoked! Ali lands it full outside off, Mire stands and goes through with the smack down the ground. Hits it aerially but well away from mid on. Although Sarfraz screams from behind the stumps that the fielder should catch that, it was well away from him.
Beautifully bowled. Amir saw Zhuwao make room and speared a fast yorker in line of the stumps. Cephas did well to dig it out to the off side for nothing.
Outside off on a length, dabbed towards third man for one.

Almost! Full on middle and leg, hit aerially from the crease towards mid on. It landed well short of the man there. It was almost an action replay of the way he was dismissed in the previous games against the Aussies.
Ouch! That might have hurt! Short ball around middle and leg, Mire fails in his attempted pull and takes a blow to his thigh pad.

EDGED AND FOUR! Where's the slip, Sarfraz? This is angled away on a length, Mire looks to guide it towards third man. Although he wouldn't mind the result now, he never intended to get it so fine. The outside edge was taken and the ball raced away to the third man fence.
On a length around middle and off, Mire lets it come to him and bunts it from the crease.
Fuller on the pads, Mire misses the flick. The ball goes off his pads towards backward square leg. Zhuwao calls for the run and Mire responds. A leg bye it is.
On the pads, flicked away through mid-wicket for one.

FOUR! Streaky yet effective! Full and angling away, Zhuwao looks to smash it through the on side. The ball takes the inside edge and just goes close past the leg stump and through to the fine leg fence.
Zhuwao seems to get restless pretty quickly. He has a wild swing at this full length ball outside off, only to miss it completely.
Short in length, pulled straight to mid-wicket.
FOUR! What a welcome for Hasan Ali! Fuller in length around middle and leg, Zhuwao gets his front foot out of the way and smashes it back down. It passes just past the bowler and beats mid on easily.
Hasan Ali to have a go now. Perhaps Malik's expensive first over mooted this move.
Finally a run for Cephas. Works this length ball to the on side to retain strike. Just 2 off this one.
Fuller and outside off, pushed from the crease towards covers. Another dot.
Another swish and a miss! Zhuwao seems to be getting restless. He looks to have a go at another length ball outside off. Misses the ball completely. Three dots in a row.
Length ball in line of the stumps, Zhuwao looks to flick it but misses and wears it high on the thigh pad.
No footwork! Landing on a length outside off, Zhuwao stays put in the crease and has a feel for it. Misses.
Length ball angling away, Mire slashes at it. The ball takes the outside edge and goes towards third man for one.
Mohammad Amir to bowl from the other end.
FOUR! Lovely way to end the over. Tossed up outside off, Zhuwao goes inside out through covers and gets a boundary. 12 off the opening over for Zimbabwe, 10 off the last three balls.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

SIX! Boom! This time Zhuwao connects alright. Slower through the air around middle, he kneels down and slogs it high and handsome over deep mid-wicket for half a dozen. Wonderful way to open the boundary count.

Huge appeal right away! Not given, though. Tossed up around middle and leg, Zhuwao looks to belt it over mid-wicket but misses. The ball hits him on the back pad and an appeal ensues. Turned down, perhaps because it is sliding down leg.
Floated from round the stumps, Mire flicks it towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end. He too, opens his account.

Flatter one on the pads, Zhuwao works it towards square leg and sets off for a run. The man from mid-wicket takes just that extra bit of time to get across and return the throw to Sarfraz, which doesn't please the Pakistan skipper. Zimbabwe and Cephas get off the mark.

Blue skies and sunny conditions welcome the players onto the ground. But the players observe a minute of silence to mourn the passing away of the wife of former South African cricketer, Gary Brent. Cephas Zhuwao and Solomon Mire walk out to bat, hoping to get the home side off to a flier. The Men in Green have spread out all over the field, in readiness for play to commence. Shoaib Malik will have a go with the new ball, from round the wicket. Here we go...

Hamilton Masakadza, the Zimbabwe captain, says that he expects the track to be dry and doesn't mind batting first. States that they were pretty ordinary in the last game and would look to correct the mistakes. Adds that the guys are raring to go and are all set.

Sarfraz Ahmed, the Pakistan captain, reasons that they want to make use of the conditions early on. States that they will look to forget about the last game against Australia and look to turn up afresh.

Dirk Vijleon does the PITCH REPORT. He says that the track is the same as the last game. Reckons that not much damage has been done, thereby stating that it is a good hard pitch. Adds that there is not too much grass but a few cracks opening up. States that it is important for the bowlers to land the cherry in the right areas.

TEAM CHANGES - For Pakistan, Mohammad Amir plays and so does Haris Sohail. Mohammad Hafeez and Usman Khan make way for them. Cephas Zhuwao, Malcolm Waller and Wellington Masakadza come to the playing XI in place of Chamu Chibhabha, Ryan Burl and John Nyumbu for Zimbabwe. Well, the hosts may well hope that the team changes help them change the result as well.
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of the touring side. PAKISTAN OPT TO CHASE!

Pakistan have seldom put a false foot in the shortest format in recent times, with their previous outing against the Aussies not going their way after 8 straight T20I wins. They will quickly look to shrug off that game out of their memories, by attempting to inflict another heavy defeat on the hosts. Is that the script for the day? Remember, this is the second leg of this series. We'll find out soon. Hold on for a while.

Often when you're pushed back to the wall, the urge to fight back and retaliate in full force is greater. Zimbabwe have always been the perennial underdogs in the cricketing world. With two heavy defeats, they just asserted that tag. Till recently, they were lauded for their competing efforts, but with most of their 'known' personnel missing out, they have been largely pedestrian to say the least. With another hope of this being a thrilling clash, here's a warm welcome to y'all for the 4th game of the T20I tri-series featuring Australia and Pakistan, apart from the hosts, in Harare.
